topics.topic: Required input and expected-output port coverage for trial cases
questions: Must inputs name every input port and no others, and when `expected_outputs` is present must it name every output port and no others?
Must inputs contain exactly every input port and no extra names, and when expected outputs are present must they contain exactly every output port, or may expected outputs assert only a subset?
Must an authored trial case supply exactly one value for every contract input and no unknown inputs?
When expected_outputs is present, is it a complete expected result or may it specify only a subset of output ports?

quotes:
### Inputs

A contract version, input values by port, optional expected outputs, the actor.

### Enforces

Fit in port name order — presence, carriage, schema, size; inputs take the
port's class, expected outputs the highest class of the inputs (A04 rule 1,
M21).
judgement.why: These passages were unchanged by the reopening change, which only renamed store changes and refined persistence-module ownership.

topics.topic: Allowed API base URL forms and operation-path joining rules
questions: May `api_base_url` contain user information, a path prefix, query, fragment, percent escapes or multiple trailing slashes, and exactly how is it joined to the operation path?
Are user information, query, fragment and multiple trailing slashes allowed in api_base_url, and precisely how are they combined with the operation path?

judgement.why: This is the same question about accepted base-URL forms and exact path joining, and neither its passages nor the reopening change altered it.

precedent.topic: Allowed HTTP base URLs and exact request-URL joining behavior
quotes:
the installation selects no instance for the service or that
   instance has no `api_base_url` — one that is not an absolute `http` or
   `https` URL with a host counts as none — or names one required header
   twice, or names one the kernel sets itself (`host`, `accept-encoding`,
   `content-type`, `content-length`, A10 rule 7) other than `host`, which an
   instance may set instead of the kernel (A10 rule 7), names compared without
   regard to case — at send time both are A09 rule 6's `required_header_repeated`
   —, or has a required header whose name is not an HTTP field-name token, or whose value is empty, has leading or trailing whitespace, or holds a control character — at send time `required_header_invalid`;

The
   URL is the `api_base_url` without a trailing `/` followed by the declared
   path, which must start with one `/` and contain no `//`, no `.` or `..`
   segment, no `?` or `#`, and no scheme or host; a `{` or `}` appears only in a
   placeholder, which is one whole segment `{name}` whose name is not empty and
   contains no `{`, `}` or `/`, and no name is a placeholder twice; a path that
   does not is not invocable (A08 rule 3). Placeholder values are percent-encoded so that they
   stay one segment. Nothing else is normalized.

Plain `http` is allowed only for an instance of
   class `local_dev` or `disposable_rig`, as the manifest instance's `class`
   states — an absent or unknown class counts as `production` — or one whose
   `api_base_url` host is a loopback address; any other plain `http` target is refused before sending.
   The host judged here, the one connected to, and for `https` the server name
   sent and verified, are always those of `api_base_url`; a required `Host`
   header (A10 rule 7) changes only the header sent.

`host` — the authority of `api_base_url` exactly as the manifest writes it,
   not normalized (A09 rule 1), unless the instance's required headers name
   `host`, in which case that required header is sent instead, its value
   verbatim, and is the only `host` —, `accept-encoding: identity` (A09 rule 3),
precedent.why: The texts constrain an absolute HTTP(S) URL and simple concatenation but do not close the accepted URL grammar, slash handling, component interaction, or loopback classification.

topics.topic: Error classification for missing references in captured trial cases
questions: If the implementation, source execution, contract version or referenced SpooledFile is missing when this inter-module operation runs, is the result `unknown_reference`, `refused`, or `internal_error` because its caller was expected to pass existing records?
If the implementation or a referenced SpooledFile is missing, does this operation return `unknown_reference`, `refused`, or `internal_error` because its `runs` caller supplied inconsistent facts?

quotes:
A missing record is `unknown_reference`
  naming it, whatever operation looked it up.

### Errors

`refused` naming the first failing check.
judgement.why: The missing-reference and captured-case error passages were unchanged, and the persistence refactor did not make their classification newly consequential.

topics.topic: Filesystem privacy and symlink checks performed when opening the store
questions: What ownership and permission bits make the data directory and its contents private, and are symbolic links rejected only inside the data directory, in the data-directory path itself, or in every ancestor component too?

Which ownership and permission checks apply at start: only to the data directory, or recursively to every existing database, value, fixture, spool and lock entry, and what exact permissions count as private?

quotes:
### Errors

`refused` naming a data directory that does not exist, the lock held, a
directory not private, or a symbolic link; the start stops. The kernel never
creates the data directory itself: the owner creates it, private to the
kernel's user; inside it `open_store` creates the database schema, the
content-addressed area and the spool area when absent.
judgement.why: The reopening change did not touch the open-store privacy or symbolic-link requirements or make their scope newly relevant.

topics.topic: Immutable manifest record resolution at a revision and symlink handling
questions: How is a file read “at” a revision: from a Git object, from a checked-out directory whose revision is verified, or through another immutable snapshot mechanism?
What exact object is read for a manifest record at a revision, and how are symlink entries or symlinked path components handled?

quotes:
### Outputs

The manifest location and revision fixed at start (M28).

The kernel reads a service's record only from
`<manifest_location>/<service_id>.json` at the configured `manifest_revision`
(M28), and only when the file's `service` field equals `service_id`. No other
path, revision or name is searched.
judgement.why: The manifest-revision and record-resolution passages were unchanged by the persistence-module and store-change-name edits.

topics.topic: Preserving and rejecting duplicate JSON object keys during canonicalization
questions: Which module parses the original JSON text and detects duplicate object names before they are lost in an ordinary decoded JSON value?
How can this operation observe and refuse duplicate object keys after its input has already become a JSON value, whose object representation normally cannot retain duplicate keys?

judgement.why: This is the same duplicate-key detection and canonical-input parsing question, and neither the quoted passages nor the reopening change altered it.

precedent.topic: Canonical JSON input parsing, duplicate-key detection, and surface refusal translation
quotes:
`module:surface` turns every JSON text a
  request carries — a value, a port's `value_schema`, a guard value — into its
  canonical form with `canonical_values.canonical_bytes` before any module
  sees it; a text JCS cannot represent is `invalid_request` (A01 rule 1:
  refused where it enters).

`module:canonical_values`. Encode one value as RFC 8785 canonical JSON bytes, or refuse a value JCS cannot
represent.
precedent.why: These passages were unchanged by the reopening change, which concerned persistence-module ownership and store-change names.

topics.topic: Scope and ordering of installed-capability validation at startup
questions: Which exact subset of A08 rule 5 is a check “of the record itself” at startup, and can a malformed capability unrelated to the selected instance or credential stop the kernel?
With no operation name or proposal ports supplied, which operation-specific A08 checks must this start operation apply, to which capability entries, and in what order?

judgement.why: This is the same question about the subset and ordering of startup manifest validation, unchanged by the reopening change.

precedent.topic: Scope of A08 rule 5 validation during installed-instance startup checks
quotes: read_service_record: [VALIDATION_ERROR] Raises RefusedError naming the first failing check of the record itself, in this order: the record is absent at that revision, is not valid JSON, lacks service or capabilities, its service field differs from service_id, two capabilities share a name.

check_installed_instances: [VALIDATION_ERROR] Takes the services the installation holds a credential for, in service_id order by Unicode code point, and for each raises RefusedError naming that service at the first failure: first the credential header name equals a name in the imported KERNEL_SET_HEADER_NAMES constant compared without regard to case, host included, checked without reading the manifest; then, only when the installation selects an instance for the service, its record read by read_service_record fails any check, or the selected instance named in the record has a required header whose name equals the credential header name compared without regard to case.

check_installed_instances: [BEHAVIOR] A service with no selected instance, or whose record lists no instance of the selected name, fails nothing here; the check reads only the given installation and the manifest, never the store, and returns None when every service passes.
precedent.why: The later notes limit startup validation to credential-bearing services, ordered by service_id, and to top-level service-record checks plus the selected instance's credential-header collision.

topics.topic: Agent-code access to runtime and exchange-directory files
questions: May agent code itself read runtime files and read or write arbitrary paths inside the exchange directory, or are those paths available only to the sandbox runner for transporting inputs and outputs?

topics.topic: Atomicity of admission verdict persistence and automatic activation
questions: Are an admitted verdict and its automatic Activation committed atomically, or may the verdict remain committed if the later activation write fails?

topics.topic: Disclosure class of mapped outputs when mapped input is empty
questions: What class can the proof assume for a mapped operation's output when the mapped input may be empty?

topics.topic: Encoding or rejection of multipart port names and filenames
questions: How are quotes, backslashes, non-ASCII characters and control characters in a port name encoded or refused when used as multipart name and filename parameters?

topics.topic: Exact sandbox probe program and success criteria
questions: What exact program, ports, inputs, bounds and success conditions constitute the probe execution?

topics.topic: Identity recipe, sorting rules, and meaning of one canonical value
questions: How does the operation know which identity recipe and list-sorting rules to apply, and does “one value” mean its raw `value_digest` or the M21 `value_id` derived from digest, schema, carriage, media type and class?

topics.topic: MCP transport, endpoint, token placement, and request-size accounting
questions: Which MCP transport and endpoint are served, where the token is carried, and which bytes constitute the request message for `surface_request_bytes_max`?

topics.topic: Multipart boundary generation and collision prevention
questions: How must prepare_request choose a multipart boundary and prevent it from colliding with part content?

topics.topic: Representation, ownership, retention, and reuse of prepared service requests
questions: Is the prepared request an opaque, non-inspectable capability owned by `service_invoker`, or a request structure containing the credential that crosses into `effects`; and may it be retained or reused?

topics.topic: Surface representation and disclosure masking of trial execution outputs
questions: What exactly does `try_implementation`, `list_records` for TrialExecutions and the repair view return for value outputs and file outputs, and how is a trial file output's disclosure class supplied for agent masking?

topics.topic: Unit used to measure masked failure-detail length
questions: Is the disclosed failure_detail length measured in UTF-8 bytes, Unicode code points, or another unit?

topics.topic: Whether store startup removes orphaned content-addressed values
questions: Does `open_store` remove unreferenced content-addressed value bytes, or only temporary files?
